chapter_mapping: The unit is chapter C1 Air and water in full: L1 = C1.1 (atmosphere over time), L2 = C1.2 (temperature changes in reactions), L3 = C1.3 (climate change), L4 = C1.4 (potable water). J258 has eight teaching chapters C1-C8 (C7 Ideas about Science, C8 Practical Skills), not C1-C6 plus CS7.
assessment_structure: Four externally assessed components, 100% external. Breadth in chemistry = 01 Foundation and 03 Higher; Depth in chemistry = 02 Foundation and 04 Higher. Each is 90 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 50% of that tier. Both Breadth and Depth assess content from across all teaching chapters 1 to 8, so there is no paper-by-topic split. Depth carries at least two 6-mark extended-response questions; Breadth carries none. No lesson in this unit makes any paper claim, so nothing needed correcting on that count.
tier_rule: Bold content statements only are Higher Tier. In C1 the only Higher-only statements are C1.1 outcome 2 (limitations of the particle model with inelastic spheres) and C1.2 outcome 5 plus its narrative sentence (calculating energy changes from bond energies). C1.3 and C1.4 contain no bold content at all.

findings.claim: A full section ("The Ozone Layer — A Shield for Life on Land", plus ozone passages in n10 and n15), the 6-mark extended-response practice question and a flashcard are all built on the ozone layer.
findings.truth: The word "ozone" does not appear anywhere in the J258 Chemistry B specification. C1.1 outcome 6 asks only for how an oxygen-rich atmosphere developed over time. The highest-value practice item in the lesson is therefore spent on content this board never assesses. Per the unit brief, out-of-scope material is labelled, not deleted: the exam tip now flags it as background and the practice question carries a background prefix.
findings.evidence: grep -i "ozone" specs/ocr/chemistry-b-21c-J258.md returns no matches; spec C1.1 outcomes 1-13

findings.claim: The <dfn> definition of nitrogen says the gas "was built up gradually as volcanic gases accumulated and biological nitrogen fixation recycled it".
findings.truth: Nitrogen fixation removes N2 from the air; it converts it to ammonia and nitrates. Denitrification is what returns N2 to the atmosphere. The lesson's own prose (n18) and its glossary entry both say "biological nitrogen cycling", so the tooltip contradicts them. One-phrase fix inside a data-def attribute; no narration block is touched.
findings.evidence: settled fact; lesson glossary_terms[0] and content n18 already say "cycling"

findings.claim: Question 4 is typed "4 marks — Compare or Contrast" but asks "Explain two ways in which carbon dioxide was removed from the early atmosphere."
findings.truth: The task is an explain, not a comparison. The 4-mark allocation and the four-point mark scheme are both sound. Belongs in the question-type relabel queue rather than this pass.

findings.claim: Question 5 ("Explain in terms of bond breaking and bond making why an exothermic reaction releases energy to the surroundings.") is typed "3 marks — Explain (HT)".
findings.truth: This is both-tier content. In the -bold spec the C1.2 narrative "Atoms are rearranged in chemical reactions... Breaking bonds requires energy (the activation energy) whilst making bonds gives out energy" is NOT bold, and outcomes 1-4 are not bold either. Only outcome 5, "calculate energy changes in a chemical reaction by considering bond breaking and bond making energies", is bold and therefore Higher only, and the lesson already wraps that calculation correctly in higher-only. The (HT) tag tells Foundation students to skip a question they will be asked.
findings.evidence: spec -bold C1.2 lines 1089-1171: outcomes 1-4 plain, outcome 5 bold; spec tiering note "Statements shown in bold type will only be tested in the Higher Tier papers"

findings.claim: The lesson calls the diagram an "energy profile diagram" throughout (heading, dfn, key fact, exam tip, knowledge checks, flashcards) and never gives the spec's name for it.
findings.truth: The spec's term is "reaction profile": C1.2 outcome 2 is "draw and label a reaction profile for an exothermic and an endothermic reaction, identifying activation energy". The string "energy profile" does not occur in the spec at all. A student who has only met one name can lose time on an exam question that uses the other. Fixed by naming both once in n12; the rest of the lesson is left alone.
findings.evidence: grep -i "reaction profile" spec, lines 1401, 1443, 4569; grep -i "energy profile" returns no matches

findings.claim: "Give one everyday example of an exothermic reaction." is answered "Combustion of fuels (e.g. burning methane) or neutralisation."
findings.truth: The question asks for one example and the answer offers two. Not wrong, within the 30-word limit, and no duplicate answers anywhere in the lesson. Recorded only.

findings.claim: Question 3 ("Explain why scientists use multiple independent lines of evidence when building a case for climate change.") is typed "3 marks — Explain (HT)".
findings.truth: Topic C1.3 contains no bold statements at all. Every narrative sentence and all six outcomes are plain text, so the whole topic is assessed at both tiers. There is no Higher-only climate-change content on this board. The tag also contradicts the lesson itself, which is tier "both" and carries no higher-only wrapper.
findings.evidence: spec -bold C1.3 lines 1172-1268: no bold content statements

findings.claim: The unit brief flagged a possibly garbled dash in the lesson 3 title.
findings.truth: No fault. The live title is "Climate Change — Evidence and Response" and the character is U+2014 EM DASH, correct and consistent with the rest of the corpus. The garbling was a Windows console encoding artefact when the title was printed, not stored data. No edit.

findings.claim: The lesson names a "required practical" in five places: the h2 reads "Analysing Water Samples (Required Practical)", n15 opens "The required practical for this topic...", the exam tip says "In required practical questions...", the takeaway says "The required practical involves...", and practice question 5 is typed "4 marks — Required Practical Method".
findings.truth: This board has no required practicals. J258 uses Practical Activity Groups, PAG1 to PAG8, and learners must complete a minimum of eight practicals covering the listed apparatus and techniques. The phrase "required practical" does not appear once in the specification. The practical the lesson then describes (flame tests, silver nitrate for chloride ions) is chapter C5 Chemical analysis, PAG5 work, not C1.4, so "the required practical for this topic" is wrong twice over. Terminology corrected in all five places; the activity itself is kept and reframed as a practical activity, not deleted.
findings.evidence: spec practical section lines 12140-12340 (PAG1 to PAG8; "Learners must complete a minimum of eight practicals"); grep -i "required practical" returns no matches; C5 outcomes 5-7 lines 3919-3936 = flame tests and acidified dilute silver nitrate, PAG5

findings.claim: The lesson teaches "three main stages" in a fixed order, filtration then sedimentation then sterilisation, and the exam tip instructs students to "use the correct sequence".
findings.truth: Not corrected. The order matches the common GCSE textbook model (coarse filtration and screening first, then coagulation and settlement, then chlorination), so it is defensible teaching and I am not certain enough to reverse it. But this board asks for methods, not a sequence: C1.4 outcome 1 lists "filtration and membrane filtration; aeration, use of bacteria; chlorination and distillation (for salt water)". The word "sedimentation" never appears in the spec, and aeration, which does, is not covered anywhere in the unit. Flagged for the coverage backlog, not for an edit.
findings.evidence: spec C1.4 outcome 1, lines 1640-1645; grep -i "sedimentation" returns no matches

findings.claim: Question 5 and its mark scheme use "silver nitrate solution" for the chloride-ion test.
findings.truth: The spec requires acidified dilute silver nitrate for the halide test. The question is about planning variables rather than describing the test, so no marks turn on it here, but the unacidified wording would be marked down in a C5 question.

findings.claim: Coverage gap: C1.4 outcome 2, "describe a test to identify chlorine (using blue litmus paper)" (PAG2), and the C1.4 practical "identify unknown gases" appear nowhere in the unit.
findings.truth: Missing content, not wrong content, so no edit under this brief. Recorded because it is an assessable outcome with a named PAG that the unit's only practical section displaces with C5 material.

summary: Four lessons checked; all are tier 'both' and correctly so, and the single higher-only wrapper (bond-energy calculations, L2) matches the one bold spec statement it should. No arithmetic is wrong: the L2 worked example H2 + Cl2 to 2HCl recomputes exactly (436 + 242 = 678; 2 x 432 = 864; 678 - 864 = -186 kJ/mol, exothermic) on correct bond energies, and CuCO3 to CuO + CO2 is balanced. All 20 knowledge check keys and all four match sets are correct, and no flashcard answer is over-length or duplicated within a lesson. The real yield is exam framing rather than science: two practice questions tagged (HT) that are both-tier content, AQA-style 'required practical' language across a lesson on a board that only has PAGs, ozone-layer material this specification never mentions, and the spec's own term 'reaction profile' absent from the energy lesson.
